name: sei-site-auditor
description: SEI Site Auditor — AEM asset auditing, reverse image search, testimonial management, and video intake for capella.edu

scripts.// build:packages: The shared packages must be compiled before apps/* can resolve them — `tsc --build` walks the project references in dependency order.
scripts.predev: npm run db:generate && npm run build:packages
scripts.dev: concurrently -n api,ui,worker -c blue,green,magenta "npm run dev:api" "npm run dev:ui" "npm run dev:worker"
scripts.// build:ui: Vercel builds only this. The UI's single workspace dependency is @capella/types, so this deliberately avoids `tsc --build` at the root — that would drag in packages/db (needs `prisma generate`) and packages/scraper (needs Playwright), neither of which a static frontend host should have to install.
scripts.// build:static: Publishes the UI with the index baked in and no backend at all. The only free, always-on option for this tool: the worker needs a persistent process and Chromium, which no free tier provides, but everything the index already knows is static.
scripts.//test: Every package is ESM, so ts-jest needs Node's ESM VM modules. Without the flag it silently downlevels to CommonJS and any file using import.meta fails to compile — three suites disappeared exactly that way.
scripts.// db:snapshot: The indexed data is the expensive part of this tool and lived only in one laptop's Postgres. A snapshot in the repo means a fresh clone comes up with real findings instead of an empty shell.

//dependencies: The prisma CLI is a RUNTIME dependency of the deployed image, not just a build tool: render.yaml runs `prisma migrate deploy` as a pre-deploy step inside the built container, where the runtime stage installs with --omit=dev. As a devDependency it was absent there, so npx would have tried to fetch it from the network mid-deploy — failing on a restricted host, or silently pulling a version that does not match the lockfile.
